messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 pager triggered: billing/usage dashboard showing ~30% undercount for a subset of customers in EU region. Affected components: metering-agg, realtime-display. Pager routed to chris_oncall and alex_sre.

chris_oncall: ack — I'm on it. starting a quick triage. pinging jin_billing for any recent deploys to aggregation pipeline.

alex_sre: joining. I see a surge of late-arriving events around the ETL window (02:00-02:15 UTC). dashboards read from agg-cache which hasn't been updated for some partitions.

jin_billing: no planned deploys in the last 24h. I did notice a config flip on the Kafka consumer group yesterday (consumer group ID changed during a migration), might be related.

maria_ops: FYI, our retention job for raw-events-archive restarted at 02:05 with backfill enabled. Could have bumped offsets.

chris_oncall: hypothesis: consumer offset drift + partition reassignment caused metering-agg to skip a window -> agg-cache stale -> UI undercounts. Can someone run a quick query to compare raw events vs agg counts for sample orgs?

alex_sre: running a diff for orgs: redwood-core, alpha-saas, horizon-inc. query:
```sql
SELECT org_id, sum(tokens) AS raw_tokens
FROM raw_tokens.daily
WHERE ts >= '2026-03-14T02:00:00Z' AND ts < '2026-03-14T03:00:00Z'
GROUP BY org_id;

SELECT org_id, sum(tokens) AS agg_tokens
FROM billing.agg_hourly
WHERE hour = '2026-03-14T02:00:00Z'
GROUP BY org_id;
```
returns: raw_tokens ~1.3M, agg_tokens ~900k for redwood-core (31% gap). matching the 30% undercount.

jin_billing: confirmed. cross-checked ledger write logs — agg job reported 'ok' but processed 63% of partitions. Missing partitions show consumer lag.

liz_cs: what's customer impact? dashboards underreport usage for customers who check invoices right now? any invoices already generated incorrectly?

chris_oncall: impact: UI "usage explorer" and invoice preview pages read from agg cache. No finalized invoices yet (billing cycle closes later). So customer bills not finalized, but previews and usage alerts wrong. Need to post a status page update and CS template asap.

ryan_product: draft status page update suggestion: "Investigating partial underreporting of usage in the Usage Dashboard for EU customers. Root cause: metering aggregation lag due to consumer offset drift. Some customers may see lower-than-expected usage in previews. We're actively recovering missing partitions and backfilling aggregated counts. No invoices have been finalized. Updates every 30 minutes." Thoughts?

maria_ops: sounds good. add ETA for next update and mitigations: that we will run a targeted backfill and re-populate agg-cache, and verify with sample queries.

chris_oncall: agreed. here's a short CS template for support reps to use: 

"Hi <customer>, we are currently investigating an issue where usage shown in the dashboard may be lower than actual for some customers in EU. We are performing a backfill of metering data and expect dashboard values to be corrected within 2–4 hours. No invoices have been finalized and you will not be billed incorrectly. We’ll follow up when counts are restored. — Redwood Support"

liz_cs: copying that into a canned response now. Also flagging top 10 affected customers so reps can proactively reach out.

alex_sre: mitigation plan: 1) pause retention job to avoid further offset shifts, 2) restart metering consumer with previous group ID to rejoin partitions, 3) run targeted backfill job for the missing hour(s) that writes to agg_hourly, 4) refresh agg-cache and bump cache version. Executing step 1 now.

chris_oncall: executing step 2 (restart consumer). Will monitor partition assignments.

deploy-bot: build 0.52.13 deployed to metering-consumer (restart initiated by chris_oncall) — restart completed. logs: partition reassign completed.

alex_sre: partition counts restored. kicking off backfill job: 
```bash
python tools/run_backfill.py --start '2026-03-14T02:00:00Z' --end '2026-03-14T03:00:00Z' --target agg_hourly --orgs-file /tmp/affected_orgs.txt
```
Estimated run: ~18 minutes for the affected partitions.

chris_oncall: good. schedule a cache refresh after backfill completes and verify diffs again. If diffs <3% for sample orgs, mark incident as mitigated and update status page to "partial mitigation - backfill complete, monitoring".

liz_cs: CS will update customers in the top 10 list once we have post-backfill verification.

maria_ops: backfill started. progress: 30% after 5m. logs show missing messages being processed and agg_hourly writes happening.

alex_sre: backfill complete. re-ran diffs: redwood-core gap now 0.8%, alpha-saas 0.4%, horizon-inc 1.1%. Acceptable.

chris_oncall: refreshing agg-cache version v297 -> v298. cache refresh completed. UI shows corrected usage values.

incident-bot: Incident status update posted to status.redwood.ai /components/usage: "Resolved (partial) - Aggregation backfill completed for affected EU partitions; dashboard counts refreshed. Customers who saw undercounts should see corrected values now. No invoices were finalized during this window. Working on postmortem and reconciliation notes."

liz_cs: sending customer update to top 10 now. template updated with actual recovery ETA.

ryan_product: please open a postmortem with timeline and root cause (consumer group id drift + retention job restart). Also include a mitigation to ensure consumer group id changes require a migration window.

chris_oncall: created incident channel #incident-1923456789 and started postmortem draft. Assigning action items: jin_billing -> add guardrails for consumer group_id changes; maria_ops -> add gating to retention restarts; alex_sre -> add an alert on agg_hourly partition coverage < 95%.

maria_ops: handing off to next oncall (eve) in 30m with notes. I'll remain available for questions.

chris_oncall: thanks team, marking the on-call handoff soon. Closing thread for active mitigation.
